newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-KPN bid for TNT at low end - BT says.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-KPN bid for TNT at low end - BT says.

text.p: Bankers Trust Australia, which has built a strategic 19.99 percent stake in TNT Ltd, said on Wednesday the A$2.45 per share cash bid for the transport firm by Koninklijke PTT Nederland was at the lower end of its range of valuations.

A BT spokeswom also told Reuters the bid by KPN, a Dutch telecoms and postal company, might have faced serious problems if TNT had not sold its half share in airline Ansett Australia one day before the friendly bid was announced last Wednesday.
BT would not say if it would accept the KPN offer.

"No comment. The bottom line is we are just waiting to see what happens, that is really what we are doing," the BT spokeswoman said when asked if the investment bank and funds manager would eventually sell its holding to KPN.
BT said it had increased its stake in TNT by 18.04 million shares to a total of 117.014 million since the bid was announced, paying less than the offer price.

"The A$2.45 bid by KPN for TNT is at a price that is at the lower end of a range of valuations we have on the company," BT executive vice-president Rohan Hedley said in a statement prepared in response to questions by Reuters.
"KPN has also indicated that the price is a good deal. KPN's own share price rose 3.5 percent on the news in their home stock exchange," said Hedley, who is head of Australian equities at BT.
"It is important to note that the bid was announced one day after the close of the sale of TNT's 50 percent interest by TNT.

"TNT's position in Ansett would have represented a significant impediment for any potential foreign acquirer," he said. Air New Zealand Ltd said in early September it would pay TNT A$325 million for its share in the struggling carrier, becoming a joint owner with News Corp Ltd.

"KPN have indicated that they expect the acquisition to be EPS (earnings per share) positive in year one and materially so in year two, despite the fact that there are relatively few obvious synergies between the majority of businesses within the two groups," Hedley said.
A spokeswoman for KPN's corporate advisers said the Dutch company was aware of the substantial shareholder notice filed by Bankers Trust after the close of trade on Tuesday.
"Yes, KPN is obviously aware of this," she said.
"It is the action of a single shareholder. KPN is not prepared to make any comment on it," she said.

KPN chairman Wim Dik, announcing the bid at a news conference alongside TNT executives, said he regarded the A$2.45 per share offer price as "full and fair". On the same day, KPN acquired a 9.9 percent stake at the offer price. This stake was acquired in about 10 minutes, one fund manager said.
The offer was 50 percent above TNT's closing price on the previous day, and was described as generous by most analysts.
A number of other funds have recently reduced their TNT holdings, including JP Morgan Investment Management. TNT shares were two cents higher at A$2.41 at 1.10 p.m. (0310 GMT).
